es.summary: Un principal eliminó con éxito una access policy de Access Context Manager o uno de sus componentes (access level, access zone o authorized orgs desc). Esto puede debilitar los controles de acceso contextual que protegen recursos de GCP.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de GCP Audit Logs del servicio accesscontextmanager.googleapis.com en los que data.protoPayload.authorizationInfo.permission es una de las cuatro operaciones de borrado (accessPolicies, accessLevels, accessZones o authorizedOrgsDescs) y granted es true.
es.why_it_matters: Access Context Manager restringe el acceso por contexto, por ejemplo por IP, dispositivo o perímetro. Si un adversario elimina estas políticas, puede abrir el acceso a recursos protegidos y mantenerlo (T1098, manipulación de cuentas y permisos).
triage_steps: Identifique al actor en data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail y determine si es un usuario humano, una service account o una identidad federada.
Revise data.protoPayload.methodName y resourceName para saber exactamente qué política, access level o componente se eliminó y a qué organización pertenece.
Verifique data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp y callerSuppliedUserAgent: compare con las IP y herramientas habituales del equipo de administración (Terraform, gcloud, consola).
Busque un ticket de cambio o una ventana de mantenimiento aprobada que justifique el borrado.
Pivote sobre el mismo principal en +/- 15 minutos: cambios de IAM (SetIamPolicy), creación de llaves de service account o accesos a datos que antes estaban protegidos.
Busque alertas anteriores del mismo principal o de la misma IP y logins inusuales en Cloud Identity o Workspace.
Determine qué recursos y proyectos protegía la política eliminada y revise los Data Access logs posteriores al borrado.
false_positives: Actividad administrativa legítima, como depurar access levels obsoletos o reorganizar políticas.
Pipelines de infraestructura como código (Terraform, Config Connector) que recrean o destruyen recursos de Access Context Manager durante un despliegue.
Pruebas o entornos de laboratorio en los que se crean y borran políticas con frecuencia.
response_steps: Confirme con el dueño del principal y con el equipo de seguridad en la nube si el cambio estaba autorizado.
Si no lo estaba, suspenda o restrinja la identidad: desactive la service account, revoque sus llaves o cierre las sesiones del usuario.
Restaure la política o el access level eliminado desde el código IaC o la configuración documentada.
Revise y revierta cualquier otro cambio de IAM o de acceso hecho por el mismo actor en la ventana del incidente.
Investigue el acceso a los recursos que quedaron desprotegidos y escale a respuesta a incidentes si hay evidencia de exfiltración.
es.severity_rationale: Nivel medio porque borrar estas políticas reduce controles de seguridad importantes, aunque los administradores también lo hacen de forma legítima y el contexto es lo que define el riesgo.

en.summary: A principal successfully deleted an Access Context Manager access policy or one of its components (access level, access zone or authorized orgs desc). This can weaken the context-aware access controls that protect GCP resources.
en.what_it_detects: GCP audit log events from accesscontextmanager.googleapis.com where data.protoPayload.authorizationInfo.permission is one of four delete operations (accessPolicies, accessLevels, accessZones, authorizedOrgsDescs) and granted is true.
en.why_it_matters: Access Context Manager restricts access by context such as IP, device or perimeter. An adversary who deletes these policies can open access to protected resources and keep it (T1098, account and permission manipulation).
triage_steps: Identify the actor in data.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail and decide whether it is a human user, a service account or a federated identity.
Check data.protoPayload.methodName and resourceName to see exactly which policy, access level or component was deleted and in which organization.
Check data.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp and callerSuppliedUserAgent against the admin team's usual IPs and tools (Terraform, gcloud, console).
Look for a change ticket or approved maintenance window that explains the deletion.
Pivot on the same principal within +/- 15 minutes: IAM changes (SetIamPolicy), service account key creation, or access to data that was previously protected.
Search for earlier alerts on the same principal or source IP, and unusual sign-ins in Cloud Identity or Workspace.
Work out which resources and projects the deleted policy protected and review Data Access logs after the deletion.
false_positives: Legitimate administrative work, such as cleaning up stale access levels or reorganizing policies.
Infrastructure-as-code pipelines (Terraform, Config Connector) that destroy or recreate Access Context Manager resources during deployments.
Test or lab environments where policies are created and deleted often.
response_steps: Confirm with the principal's owner and the cloud security team whether the change was authorized.
If it was not, suspend or restrict the identity: disable the service account, revoke its keys or end the user's sessions.
Restore the deleted policy or access level from IaC code or the documented configuration.
Review and roll back any other IAM or access changes made by the same actor during the incident window.
Investigate access to the resources left unprotected and escalate to incident response if there is evidence of exfiltration.
en.severity_rationale: Medium, because deleting these policies removes important security controls, but administrators also do it legitimately, so context decides the real risk.

positive.description: An unfamiliar user successfully deletes an access level from an IP outside the admin range.
A service account successfully deletes the whole access policy.

negative.description: An access level deletion is attempted but denied (granted false).
A granted update to an access level, not a deletion.
